text:
Leo Carlsson has 26 points in 17 games, and 18 of them have come on the power play. That is the story of his fourth NHL season: the Ducks have handed the 21-year-old the keys, he is on the ice for 89 percent of their power-play chances (up from 68 percent), and he is playing 20:10 a night. He was named the NHL's third star for the week ending November 1, and he takes a seven-game point streak into the next one.

Some of this will cool. He is shooting 22.2 percent on 27 shots, well above his range, and his teammates are finishing far better than their chances with him on the ice. Our range for his scoring rate sits around 3.2 points per 60, not the 4.55 he is producing.

What is real is the playmaking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.0 primary shot assists per 60 last season (94th percentile among forwards), carrying the puck in on 73 percent of his entries. A pass-first No. 2 overall pick who now owns the first unit is a player Anaheim builds around. Watch whether the even-strength points catch up to the power-play ones.
headline: Carlsson is running Anaheim's power play now
